newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile minister blames trade spats on protectionism.
newsitem.headline: Chile minister blames trade spats on protectionism.

text.p: Chilean Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia blamed Tuesday protectionism in the United States for trade disputes between U.S. producers and Chilean salmon raisers and forestry companies.
"I believe that there are protectionist forces in all countries... I don't hold the United States government responsible for this," Garcia told reporters.
"We believe that for (free trade) to flourish and develop, we must overcome protectionist forces which inevitably surge within countries."

Garcia said he will travel to Washington next week for talks with U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley to discuss allegations of dumping and illegal subsidies made by U.S. salmon raisers against their Chilean counterparts.
The Chilean government said last month that it will defend Chilean firms against the subsidy claims.

The spats are embarrassing for President Frei's government, which has pushed for the last two years for Chile's membership in the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) as a way of phasing out trade barriers with the U.S.

Asked whether he would raise the issue of the forestry dispute, Garcia replied: "Maybe. In my talks with Daly I will point out the trade difficulties we have, within the framework that both countries are committed to overcoming these barriers."

Chilean forestry firms denounced last month a federal court ruling which they said prohibited the U.S. government from issuing new permits for log and wood chip imports from Chile, New Zealand and Russia.
The court in San Francisco ruled in mid-June that no new permits could be authorized as wood from these countries has not been proved to be free of diseases which could infect North American species.
Local media reported Tuesday that U.S. agriculture authorities have already used the ruling to detain a ship loaded with Chilean wood at a port in the state of Maryland.
Chilean forestry firms said the order did not affect existing permits but would prevent new licenses from being issued in 1998.
